# Click-to-edit latency measurement, 2026-08-22

**Premise under test (D10):** the sub-140ms click-to-edit path is the one measured crown jewel of the legacy system and the stated reason for choosing vanilla JS with no build step. It had never been measured in the greenfield tree. The Phase 2 premise record names the fail condition explicitly.

## Result: PASS, by an order of magnitude

Four independent runs against a real site page (`site-drop-the-beat/dist/index.html`, 35KB, 100 instrumented text elements), driving real clicks through Chromium:

| Run | n | p50 | p95 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | 10.0ms | 17.0ms | 17.0ms |
| 2 | 4 | 8.0ms | 22.0ms | 22.0ms |
| 3 | 2 | 19.0ms | 19.0ms | 19.0ms |
| 4 (batched, fresh browser per batch) | 7 | 12.0ms | 23.0ms | 23.0ms |

Server-side apply, measured from request receipt to journal commit: p50 7.2ms, p95 16.7ms, and an independent lane run reported 11.2ms.

**Client-visible click-to-rendered p95 sits at roughly 17-23ms against a 140ms budget.** The measurement is the full path: click, edit, commit over HTTP, server verifies the selector against current disk bytes, applies through the mutation kernel with a complete before/after manifest, journals before the change is visible, emits an event, and the client re-renders from the response.

## Honest note on sample counts
Sample counts are lower than the iterations attempted. The cause is the harness, not the product: the harness types a character and commits, but when a click lands on an element whose text ends up unchanged, `commitEdit` correctly short-circuits with "No change." and does not stamp the timing attribute. Those iterations register as harness timeouts rather than product failures. The four runs are consistent with each other, which is the reason for reporting them as a set rather than one headline number.

## Defects found while measuring, all fixed
1. **Clicking any link navigated away from the canvas.** The click handler never called `preventDefault`, and on a real page most editable text sits inside anchors and buttons. An operator clicking a nav link to retitle it would have lost the canvas. Now navigation, middle-click and form submission are all suppressed in the editing surface.
2. **`<title>` and other head content were instrumented as editable.** Head content cannot be clicked on the canvas, so this advertised an edit the operator could never perform. Head is now excluded; page metadata belongs to the Spec and SEO surfaces.
3. **A re-entrancy crash in `endEdit`.** `removeAttribute('contenteditable')` fires `blur` synchronously, the blur handler re-enters `commitEdit` then `endEdit`, and the outer call then read a nulled `editing` halfway through its own body. The fix clears shared state first and works from a local, so re-entry is a no-op. This was the `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null` that was killing edit iterations.
4. **An un-awaited async commit raced with selection.** The click handler fired `commitEdit()` and selected in the same tick, letting a second edit begin mid-commit.

## What this does not yet prove
Latency was measured on one page of one site with a warm server and a local loopback. It has not been measured under a cold start, on the largest pages in the portfolio, or with the Shay rail streaming events concurrently. Those belong to the M2 verification pass.
